VIA ELECTRONIC SUBMISSION
Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, N.E.
Washington, DC 20426

Re:        Switched On, LLC, Docket No. ER27-____

           NOTICE OF CHANGE IN STATUS AND TARIFF AMENDMENTS

Dear Secretary Reese:

        Pursuant to Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”)
Order Nos. 6521 and 860,2 along with Section 35.42 of the Commission’s regulations,3 Switched
On, LLC (“Seller”) hereby submits this Notice of Change in Status (“Notice”) to reflect a change
to the facts relied upon by the Commission in granting Seller’s market-based rate (“MBR”)
authority that occurred during the third quarter of 2026.

        Specifically, this Notice is filed to report a new ultimate upstream affiliate and affiliations
as a result of a transaction that was consummated on September 30, 2026. On August 24, 2026,
in Docket No. EC26-67-000, the Commission issued an order pursuant to Section 203 of the
Federal Power Act (“FPA”) approving a change of control of Seller and other public utility
subsidiaries of DigitalBridge Group, Inc. (“DigitalBridge”) through the indirect acquisition of
DigitalBridge by a subsidiary of SoftBank Group Corp. (“SoftBank”) (the “Transaction”).4 The
Transaction was consummated on September 30, 2026.5

       As demonstrated herein, the Transaction and new affiliations do not result in any market
power concerns and Seller continues to satisfy the Commission’s requirements for MBR
authorization.

generation in the Southwest region. Pursuant to FPA Section 205,6 Seller also submits for filing
a revised MBR Tariff that reflects a change in its Category Status to Category 2 Seller status in
the Southwest region and incorporates other conforming changes, consistent with Commission
precedent. Seller has also submitted updates to the MBR Database to reflect these changes.

      In accordance with Order No. 860, Seller provides the following reference to its asset
appendix: 74758.

II.      DESCRIPTION OF SELLER AND RELEVANT AFFILIATES

         A.       Seller

        Seller, a Nevada limited liability company, is a power marketer with market-based rate
authorization to make wholesale sales of capacity, energy, and specified ancillary services in all
regions.7 Seller does not purchase any energy and/or capacity from an unaffiliated third party
pursuant to a long-term firm agreement reportable under Order Nos. 816 and 860.8 Seller does
not own or control any facilities that are used for generation of electricity or the transmission of
electricity in interstate commerce in the United States or outside the United States that can be
used to reach markets in the United States, and Seller does not own or control any inputs to
electric power production in the United States, as defined in section 35.36(a)(4) of the
Commission’s regulations,9 including intrastate natural gas transportation, intrastate natural gas

        B.       Seller’s Upstream Ownership

         Seller is a 100% wholly owned subsidiary of Switch, Ltd. Switch, Ltd. is a privately held
data center company. Switch, Ltd. is a direct subsidiary of Switch, Inc., a Nevada corporation.
Switch, Ltd. owns various one-MW diesel generating units that are onsite at its data center
facilities for emergency back-up generation only. These generating units are held only for
emergency use and are located behind the meter and subject to stringent air quality regulations
that prevent continuous use except in the event of a force majeure event or power failure
emergency.10

         Sunshine Bidco, Inc. (“Sunshine Bidco”), a Delaware corporation, is the direct parent of
Switch, Inc. Sunshine Bidco is owned indirectly through a series of intermediate Delaware
holding companies that are wholly owned by Sunshine Parent, LP (“Sunshine Parent”), a
Delaware limited partnership that aggregates the ownership interests of (i) DigitalBridge Partners
II, LP (including related investment vehicles and co-investment partnerships managed by
affiliates of DigitalBridge, collectively, the “DBRG Partnerships”), a Delaware limited
partnership and an investment fund managed by an affiliate of DigitalBridge, and (ii) funds
managed or advised by IFM Investors Pty Ltd (“IFM Investors”).11 The only entities that own
10% or more of the voting equity interests in Sunshine Parent are the DBRG Partnerships and
IFM Sunshine Holdings LP.

         Each of the DBRG Partnerships with ownership interests in Sunshine Parent is controlled
by general partners each of which is a Delaware limited liability company that is indirectly and
wholly owned by DigitalBridge Operating Company, LLC (“DBOC”), a Delaware limited
liability company that is approximately 97% owned by DigitalBridge. IFM Sunshine Holdings
LP is wholly owned and controlled by IFM Global Infrastructure Fund (“IFM Fund”).

       Sunshine Parent is controlled by its general partner, Sunshine Acquisition Holdings GP,
LLC (“Sunshine Acquisition GP”), a Delaware limited liability company. The only entities that
own or control 10% or more of the voting equity interests in Sunshine Acquisition GP are (i) DB
Sunshine Parent LP, the general partnership in which is held by DB Sunshine Parent GP, LLC,
which is owned by DigitalBridge II GP, LLC, which is owned by DigitalBridge DBP II Holdco,
LLC, which is in turn owned by DBOC and (ii) IFM Sunshine Holdings LP.

                   1.       DigitalBridge

        DigitalBridge is a Maryland corporation and a leading global-scale digital infrastructure
firm that invests, directly and through portfolio companies, across five key verticals: data
centers, cell towers, fiber networks, small cells and edge infrastructure with its headquarters in
Boca Raton, Florida and key offices in New York, Los Angeles, London, Luxembourg, and
Singapore. DigitalBridge conducts substantially all of its activities and holds substantially all of
its assets and liabilities through an operating subsidiary, DBOC.

        On August 24, 2026, in Docket No. EC26-67-000, the Commission issued an order
pursuant to FPA Section 203 approving a change of control of Seller through the indirect
acquisition of DigitalBridge by a subsidiary of SoftBank (i.e., the Transaction).12 As noted, the
Transaction was consummated on September 30, 2026. Following the consummation of the
Transaction, DigitalBridge and its direct subsidiary DBOC became indirect subsidiaries of
SoftBank. SoftBank holds the investment in DigitalBridge through SoftBank Group Overseas
GK, a wholly owned subsidiary of SoftBank, Duncan Holdco, LLC (“Duncan Holdco”), a
wholly owned subsidiary of SoftBank Group Overseas GK, Duncan Holdco’s subsidiary Duncan
Holdco II LLC (“Duncan Holdco II”)13, and Duncan Holdco II’s subsidiary Duncan Holdco III
LLC (“Duncan Holdco III”). Duncan Holdco, Duncan Holdco II, and Duncan Holdco III are
Delaware limited liability companies established for SoftBank investments in the United States
that have no independent operations of their own.

        SoftBank is a strategic investment holding company that holds interests in a portfolio of
diverse companies with outstanding technologies and business models in their respective fields.
SoftBank’s shares are publicly traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Masayoshi Son,
SoftBank’s founder, CEO and Chairman, directly and indirectly holds 10 percent or more of
SoftBank’s outstanding voting securities. To the best of Seller’s knowledge, Seller is not aware
of any other investor or investor group, besides Mr. Son, that directly or indirectly owns,
controls, or holds with power to vote, 10 percent or more of SoftBank’s outstanding voting
securities.14 As a result, Mr. Son has been identified as Seller’s ultimate upstream affiliate with
respect to SoftBank.

                  2.       IFM

        As noted above, IFM Sunshine Holdings LP is wholly owned and controlled by IFM

 III.     NOTICE OF CHANGE IN STATUS

       As a result of the consummation of the Transaction, Seller is now affiliated with the
SoftBank Public Utilities. Seller is submitting this Notice in compliance with the Commission’s
requirement that MBR sellers demonstrate their continued eligibility to make market-based sales
following a change to the facts originally relied upon by the Commission in granting MBR
authorization.

             A. Seller Continues to Lack Horizontal Market Power

         The Commission reviews horizontal market power by assessing the market power of the
seller and any of its affiliates that own or control generation in the relevant geographic market.24
The Commission has indicated that the relevant geographic market is the BAA or submarket, as
applicable, where the seller’s generation is physically located,25 or in the case of power
marketers, if the seller has no physical generation assets the Commission evaluates the seller’s
affiliated generation owner’s market power.26 Accordingly, with respect to the Transaction, the
relevant geographic market for Seller is the CAISO BAA, where all of the SoftBank Public
Utilities are located.27

        The affiliation between Seller and the SoftBank Public Utilities raises no horizontal
market power concerns. The Transaction did not result in a new combination of electric
generating facilities that could have an impact on the competition in the CAISO BAA as the
Transaction did not create any new affiliations with entities that own or control electric
generation in the same geographic markets. Seller is a power marketer that does not own or
control any generation. Moreover, the Commission recently determined that the market power
analysis for the SoftBank Public Utilities in the CAISO BAA satisfies the Commission’s
horizontal market power requirements.28 Seller commits to comply with all applicable CAISO
rules regarding market monitoring and mitigation.29 The Commission generally does not require

             B. Seller Continues to Lack Vertical Market Power

        The Transaction and affiliation reported herein also do not raise vertical market power
concerns. Seller and its affiliates do not own or control transmission facilities that are used for
the transmission of electricity in interstate commerce in the United States or outside of the
United States that can be used to reach markets in the United States, other than the limited and
discrete interconnection facilities required to connect individual generation facilities to the
transmission grid. Such interconnection facilities are limited and discrete facilities that qualify
for the blanket waivers provided in Section 35.28(d)(2), promulgated by Order No. 807.31

        Further, neither Seller nor its affiliates own or control any inputs to electric generation
such as intrastate natural gas transportation, storage or distribution facilities, sites for generation
capacity development, or physical sources of coal supplies or transportation for coal supplies. In
addition, neither Seller nor its affiliates are affiliated with a franchised public utility. Finally,
Seller affirms that Seller and its affiliates have not erected barriers to entry in the relevant
markets and will not erect barriers to entry in any geographic market.

IV.      TARIFF AMENDMENTS

         Seller is revising its MBR Tariff because of the need to change the seller Category in the
Southwest Region. The Commission’s regulations define a “Category 1 Seller” as a seller that
“(i) [i]s either a wholesale power marketer that controls or is affiliated with 500 MW or less of
generation in aggregate per region or a wholesale power producer that owns, controls or is
affiliated with 500 MW or less of generation in aggregate in the same region as its generation
assets; (ii) [d]oes not own, operate or control transmission facilities other than limited equipment
necessary to connect individual generating facilities to the transmission grid (or has been granted
waiver of the requirements of Order No. 888, FERC Stats. & Regs. ¶ 31,036); (iii) [i]s not
affiliated with anyone that owns, operates or controls transmission facilities in the same region as
the Seller’s generation assets; (iv) [i]s not affiliated with a franchised public utility in the same
region as the Seller’s generation assets; and (v) [d]oes not raise other vertical market power
issues.”32 Category 2 Sellers means any sellers not in Category 1.33

        As a result of Seller’s affiliation with the SoftBank Public Utilities resulting from the
Transaction, Seller changes from a Category 1 Seller to a Category 2 Seller in the Southwest
region, as Seller is now affiliated with more than 500 MW of generation in the Southwest region.

         Seller is also making non-substantive conforming changes to its Tariff consistent with
Commission precedent. In particular, Seller is revising its Tariff to delete references to section
141.14 of the Commission’s regulations, which has been removed from the Commission’s
regulations.34 Seller is also revising its Tariff to insert the docket number under which Seller
was granted MBR authorization.35

        Seller respectfully requests waiver of the 60-day prior notice filing requirement in order
to permit the revised Tariff to become effective on October 31, 2026, which is one day after this
filing. Good cause exists for granting such waiver, because the proposed tariff changes will have
no substantive effect on rates.36

V.      DOCUMENTS INCLUDED

            This transmittal letter
            Attachment A – Switched On, LLC – Revised Tariff Records (Clean and Marked)

VI.     CONCLUSION

        As discussed above, the Transaction does not materially change the facts and
circumstances that the Commission relied upon in granting MBR authority to Seller. Therefore,
Seller respectfully requests that the Commission accept this Notice for filing and find that no
further inquiry is necessary. Further, Seller respectfully requests that the Commission accept its
revised MBR Tariff for filing, effective October 31, 2026.

        If you have any questions regarding this filing, please contact the undersigned.



                                                     Respectfully submitted,


                                                         /s/

                                     Market-Based Rate Tariff

1.   Availability
     Switched On, LLC (“Seller”) makes electric energy, capacity and ancillary services
     available under this tariff to any purchaser, except as prohibited below.
2.   Rates
     All sales shall be made at the rates established by agreement between the purchaser and
     Seller.
3.   Other Terms and Conditions
     All other terms and conditions shall be established by agreement between the purchaser and
     Seller.
4.   Ancillary Services
     Seller may offer for sale those ancillary services in those markets specified and authorized
     by the Commission from time to time in orders extending such authority to all sellers
     authorized to sell electric energy and capacity at market-based rates, including:
     a. PJM: Seller offers regulation and frequency response service, energy imbalance service,
